If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over last 5 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% in mid-horizon (days 15–25) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment includes recent negative spikes (≤0.33) within last 3 days, add 1.0–2.0% downward bias in late-horizon (days 25–30) to correct for reversal risk.  
When sentiment swings from positive to negative over last 3 days, shift forecast peak downward by 2–3% in mid-horizon (days 15–25) to reflect sentiment volatility.  
If sentiment is uniformly low (≤0.33) across last 5 days, apply 2–3% upward bias in early-horizon (days 1–10) to counteract underestimation bias.  
For forecasts with >2 consecutive high sentiment values, reduce forecast slope in late-horizon (days 25–30) by 0.5–1.0% to prevent over-leverage on momentum.  
If sentiment shows strong upward trend (≥0.80) over last 3 days, apply 1.0–1.5% upward bias in early-horizon (days 1–10) to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
